650:
It shall be the duty of every operator providing lodging accommodations within the incorporated area of the City of Butler to collect the tax on occupants as imposed herein.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
651:
Every person engaging in, or about to engage in, the business of providing lodging accommodations, as above defined, in the special district shall immediately register said business with the Butler City Administrator, as the duly authorized representative of the City of Butler, a political subdivision of the State of Georgia. Persons engaged in such business must so register no later than thirty days after the date this section becomes effective, but such grace period for the filing of the registration after the effective date of the tax shall not relieve any person from the obligation of payment or collection of such tax on and after the date of imposition thereof.
1. The required registration hereunder shall set forth the name under which the operator transacts business or intends to transact business; the location of the place or places of business, the mailing address of the business, the principal contact person at said business and such other information as would facilitate the collection of the tax.
2. The registration shall be signed by the owner (if a natural person), by an officer (if a corporation) or a partner (if a partnership).
3. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an operator. However, a realtor offering cabins for rent shall be deemed to be one place of business and shall not require a separate registration for each cabin rented.
4. An operator offering more than one cabin or unit for rent under the same federal and state tax identification number shall be required to file the same number of returns as required by the State of Georgia for the filing of state sales tax returns.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
652:
Upon the registration of an operator as hereinabove provided, the Butler City Administrator's office shall issue to such operator a certificate of authority to collect the tax on occupant(s). Each certificate shall state the name and location of the business or person to which it relates.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
653:
All taxes levied by this article shall be due and payable to the City of Butler monthly, on or before the 20 th day of every month next succeeding each respective month in which taxes are collected, and payment shall be accompanied by return for the preceding monthly period showing the gross rent, rent from permanent residents, taxable rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for a period, and such other information as may be required by the Butler City Administrator's office or the governing authority of the City of Butler.
In the event that an operator is permitted under applicable state guidelines to make quarterly sales tax returns to the State of Georgia, said operator shall be permitted to make quarterly sales tax returns to the City of Butler, Georgia. At the time of registration, the operator shall indicate that he is permitted to make quarterly sales tax returns together with month and day said quarterly returns are due. The failure of the operator to indicate that he is permitted under applicable state statue to file quarterly reports will infer that monthly reports are due and collectable.
At the time any such report is due, the operator shall file a copy of the corresponding state sales tax return for the sole purpose of verifying the sums reported and due.
In the event an operator is permitted under applicable state guidelines to file annual excise, or lodging tax returns, to the State of Georgia, said operator is required to file monthly or quarterly returns for lodging tax to the City of Butler, Georgia.
In the event there are no rentals in a reporting period, lodging providers are required to file a return to the City of Butler, Georgia, stating they had zero rentals for the period.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
654:
No later than the 25 th day of each month, the designated representative shall deposit to the general city fund such excise taxes as have been paid under the provisions of this article, and such funds shall thereafter at the direction of the city council be expended for the promotion of the tourism industry in the City of Butler, or such funds at the direction of the city council of Butler, Georgia, may be otherwise be expended for the purpose of promoting tourism, conventions and trade shows as provided by statute.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
655:
Operators collecting the tax levied hereunder shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting, and payment of the amount due. The rate of the deduction shall be three percent of the amount due, but only if the amount due was not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
656:
The operator, in the event of operator's failure to pay tax when due, shall pay a penalty of 15 percent of the amount due plus interest on the total amount of delinquent taxes at the rate of eight and one-half percent per annum. In addition, the operator shall not be entitled to the fee allowed in section 32-14 of this article. The late penalty will be strictly enforced.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
657:
A. If any operator fails to file a return as required under the provisions of this section, the city shall make an estimate of the amount of gross rentals which are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period or periods in which the operator failed to file the return and shall be based upon any information which is or may come into the possession of the city.
B. The City Council of Butler, Georgia, a political subdivision of the State of Georgia or its designated representative(s) shall give to the operator written notice of determination as herein provided. The notice may be served personally or by mail; if by mail such service shall be addressed to the operator at his/her/its last known address as it appears on any of the city's records. Service by mail is complete when delivered by certified mail with a receipt signed by the addressee.
C. The amount of the determination made hereunder shall bear interest at the rate of three-fourths of one percent per month, or a fraction thereof, from the 20 th day of the month following the monthly period for which the amount or any portion thereof should have been returned, until the day of payment.
D. In addition, a penalty of five percent of the tax due or $5.00 whichever is greater for each 30 days or fraction thereof of delinquency, not to exceed 25 percent or $25.00 in the aggregate, whichever is greater, shall be assessed and paid by the operator to the city.
E. The estimated tax together with applicable penalties and interest may be collected utilizing any of the enforcement methods set forth in this article.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
658:
Each operator collecting a tax under the provisions of this section shall keep for a period of at least three years all records, receipts, invoices, and other pertinent papers setting forth the rental charged for each occupancy, the date or dates of occupancy, and such other information as the city may, in writing, from time to time require.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
659:
The city council or its designated representative(s) shall administer and enforce the provisions of this section for the collection of the tax herein imposed, and in so doing shall have the following powers:
1. To examine, or authorize the examination of, books, papers, records, financial reports, equipment, and other facilities of any operator subject to this article, in order to verify the accuracy of any return made, or if no return is made by the operator, to ascertain and determine the amount required to be paid.
2. To require the filing of reports by any person or persons having in their possession or custody information relating to rentals which are subject to the tax herein levied; and,
3. To allow a credit on any amount due payable from persons who paid the tax herein levied but who were erroneously or illegally subjected thereto.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
660:
At any time within three years after any tax or any portion of such tax required to be collected becomes due and payable, the city attorney, at the direction of the city council, may bring an action in a court of competent jurisdiction in the name of the city to collect such amount due together with interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees, and other legal fees incident thereto.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
661:
If any operator becomes liable for any amount required to be paid by this section and subsequent thereto sells out or quits the business, the successors or assignees of such operator shall withhold a sufficient amount of the purchase price to cover such amount due. In the event said purchaser of the business fails to withhold the required amount, he/she/it shall become personally liable for the extent of the tax owed, together with any applicable penalties and interest. Any operator or person who ceases to operate the entity under which the same is registered with the city, said operator or person must notify the Butler City Administrator's office in writing within 30 days of closing said enterprise.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
662:
A. Any person who shall do anything prohibited by this article or who shall fail to do anything required by this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, amenable to the process of the magistrate court of Taylor County and upon conviction, shall be assessed with any penalty, including fine, confinement, or both, allowed by law for the violation of county resolutions or ordinances each and every day that such violation exists shall be deemed a separate offense.
B. In order to enforce this article or to correct or abate any violation of the article, the City Council of the City of Butler, in addition to other remedies, may institute injunction, mandamus, or other appropriate action.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
663:
A. If any paragraph, subparagraph, sentence, clause, phrase, or any portion of this article shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, or if the provisions of any part of this article as applied to any particular situation or set of circumstances shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, such invalidity shall not be construed to affect the portions of this article not so held to be invalid, or the application of this article to other circumstances not so held to be invalid. It is hereby declared to be the intent of the City Council of Butler to provide separable and divisible parts, and it does hereby adopt any and all parts hereof as may not be held invalid for any reason.
B. All ordinances or resolutions or parts of ordinances or resolutions in conflict with the terms of this article are hereby repealed, but it is hereby provided that any ordinance or resolution or law which may be applicable hereto and aid in carrying out or making effective the intent, purpose and provisions hereof, which shall be literally construed to be in favor of the City of Butler is hereby adopted as part hereof.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
664:
In order to comply with the mandates of the applicable laws of the State of Georgia, an administrative fee is hereby implemented on any business or person under the purview of the within ordinance. Said administrative fee shall be in the amount of $150.00 payable annually. Said administrative fee shall be remitted to the City of Butler, before the 1 st day of January of each year that this article is in effect. The administrative fee after January 1 st will be $200.00. The City of Butler, or its designated representative, shall issue a lodging certificate to said enterprise paying said administrative fee.
(Ord. of 6-11-2019(1), § 1)
665:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Powers of local authorities concerning motor vehicles and traffic, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-371; powers of municipal courts concerning misdemeanor traffic offenses, O.C.G.A. § 40-13-21; adoption of uniform rules of the road by local authorities, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-372.
667:
The authority to make and enforce all rules and regulations governing traffic and the use of streets of the city be vehicles and pedestrians, shall be vested in the mayor and council, and the mayor and council shall have full power to designate directions to traffic, time limits, and locations for parking, reservation of parking places, maximum and minimum speeds insofar as same shall not conflict with the laws of the state, to establish through streets, truck routes, and stop crossing, and to install such street signs and indicators and markings as shall be necessary or advisable for the operation and enforcement of such rules and regulations. No such rule or regulation shall be effective unless and until appropriate signs, indicators or marking are installed.
(Prior Code, § 35-001)
668: Pursuant to the O.C.G.A. §§ 40-6-372, 40-1-1 through 40-1-5 and 40-6-1 through 40-6-395, known as the Uniform Rules of the Road, are hereby adopted as and for the traffic regulations of this municipality, with like effect as if recited in full herein.
669:
The following streets and parts of streets are hereby declared to be one-way streets and vehicular traffic shall move only in the indicated direction when signs indicating the direction of traffic are erected and maintained at every intersection where movement in the opposite direction is prohibited: Main Street from its intersection with Broad Street to its intersection with Ivey Street.
(Prior Code, § 35-003)
670:
No funeral, procession, or parade containing 50 or more persons or five or more vehicles, excepting the Armed Forces of the United States, the military forces of this state, and the forces of police and fire department, shall occupy, march, or proceed along any street except in the accordance with a permit issued by the chief of police and such other regulations as are forth in this chapter which may apply.
(Prior Code, § 35-004)
671:
A funeral composed of a procession of vehicles shall be identified as such by the display upon the outside of each vehicle of a pennant of a type designated by the chief of police, or by burning lights.
(Prior Code, § 35-005)
674:
As an aid in facilitating the movement of traffic on the streets of the city and in reducing accidents, the chief of police and the city electrician are hereby authorized and directed to place and maintain electric traffic-control devices and signals at such locations as may be designated from time to time by resolutions of the commission of the city.
(Prior Code, § 35-006)
675:
The chief of police of the city shall place and maintain, other than electrically operated, traffic control devices when and as required under this chapter and other traffic ordinances of the city to make effective the provisions of this chapter and such ordinances, and with the approval of the city manager, may place and maintain such additional traffic control devices as he may deem necessary to regulate traffic ordinances of the city or under state law, or to guide or warn traffic.
(Prior Code, § 35-007)
677:
Footnote 2:
Editor's note— Ord. adopted Oct. 8, 2019, § 1, amended Art. III and in so doing changed the title of said article from operation of vehicles to read as set out herein.
678:
A. No person shall drive a vehicle on a highway at a speed greater than reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing.
B. Where no special hazard exists, the following speeds shall be lawful, but any speed in excess of such a limit shall be prima facie evidence that the speed is not reasonable or prudent and is unlawful.
1. Fifteen miles per hour in passing hospitals and in passing school while schools are in session and in passing churches the hours of service therein.
2. Twenty-five miles per hour within the corporate limits, except as herein otherwise provided.
3. Thirty-five miles per hour within the zones designated, and when signs are posted at either end of a speed zone.
4. The fact that the speed of a vehicle is lower than the force going prima facie limits shall not receive the driver from the duty to decrease speed when approaching and crossing an intersection, when approaching a hill crest, when traveling upon any narrow or winding roadway, or by reason of when special hazard exist with respect to pedestrians or other traffic or by reason of weather or highway conditions, and speed shall be decreased as may be necessary to avoid colliding with any person, vehicle, or other conveyance on or entering the highway in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care.
(Prior Code, § 35-008)
679:
It shall be unlawful for any person to park or abandon a motor vehicle upon the streets of the city or upon the rights-of-way of the streets and allow said motor vehicle to remain parked or abandoned for more than 12 continuous hours. Parking on the street shall not impede safe travel of vehicles or emergency access.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
State Law reference— Under O.C.G.A. § 36-60-4, a local government may provide by ordinance for the removal and disposal of discarded, dismantled, wrecked, scrapped, ruined or junked motor vehicles or parts thereof.
680:
Should any sworn police officer or code enforcement officer of the city find any motor vehicle that has been parked or abandoned as aforesaid, he/she shall have the right to impound same and to have same removed from the streets of the city at the expense of the owner, and charge the owner storage.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
682:
A. It shall be unlawful for any person to park or cause to be parked any inoperable motor vehicle on public property or any private lot, tract or parcel of land or portion thereof, occupied or unoccupied, improved or unimproved, within the city. The presence of any inoperable vehicle on any property shall be deemed a public nuisance except as otherwise stated in this section. It shall be unlawful for any person to cause or maintain such a public nuisance by wrecking, dismantling, partially dismantling, rendering inoperable, abandoning or discarding any motor vehicle on the real property of another, including public property, or to permit or allow inoperable vehicles to be parked or maintained on his or its own property.
B. Subsection A. shall not apply to:
1. Any motor vehicle in an enclosed building;
2. Any motor vehicle on the premises of a business enterprise operated in a lawful manner, when necessary to the operation of such business; or
3. Any motor vehicle on property occupied and used for repair, reconditioning and remodeling of motor vehicles in conformance with the zoning ordinances of the city.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
683:
The provisions of this article shall be administered by the chief of police. In the enforcement of this article, the chief of police or any duly authorized sworn officers may enter upon the private or public property to examine a junked motor vehicle or obtain information as to the identity of a junked vehicle and to remove or cause to be removed the junked motor vehicle constituting a nuisance under this article.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
684:
When the chief of police, a sworn officer or code enforcement officer deems a junked motor vehicle to be a public nuisance, he/she shall issue a warning notice to the parties owning or in apparent possession of the motor vehicle to remove the junked motor vehicle. If the junked motor vehicle is not removed within 72 hours, the owner of the abandoned motor vehicle or owner of the land on which it is located shall be deemed guilty of an offense pursuant to this article and under section 21-040 herein, and, upon conviction, shall be punished as provided in section 1-008 and the cost of having the junked vehicle removed shall be added to the court costs.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
685:
Any person employed by the city to remove junked motor vehicles constituting a nuisance under this article has the right to enter upon private and public property to remove a junked motor vehicle.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
686:
Any person who operates a vehicle in violation of this article or who abandons or fails to properly maintain a vehicle shall be punished in accordance with section 1-008 of this Code of Ordinances in addition to any other penalty set forth herein.
(Ord. of 10-8-2019(1), § 1)
689:
On streets where white lines are shown for guidance, parking must conform with such lines. The driver must park his vehicle entirely within the boundaries designated by such lines. No person shall park and leave unattended a vehicle in a roadway other than parallel with the edge of the roadway, headed in the direction of traffic, and with the curb-side wheels of the vehicle within 12 inches of the edge of the roadway, except upon those streets which have been marked or signed for angle parking and on such streets vehicles shall be parked at the angle to the edge of the roadway indicated by such marks or signs.
(Prior Code, § 35-009)
692:
Every person riding a bicycle shall be subject to the provision of this chapter application to the driver of any vehicle except those provisions of such chapter which by their very nature can have no application.
(Prior Code, § 35-010)
693:
Any person riding upon a bicycle shall not attach the same or himself to any moving vehicle upon any roadway.
(Prior Code, § 35-011)
694:
The operator of a bicycle shall not carry any other person upon the handlebars, frame or tank, nor shall any other person ride upon such vehicle unless riding in an extra seat provided for each extra person.
(Prior Code, § 35-012)
695:
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride any bicycle at an unusual speed, or in a disorderly manner, or as to endanger the life or limb of another.
(Prior Code, § 35-013)
700:
A. All persons having homes, stores, shops, offices or places of business either as owner, tenant or occupant inside the city limits shall be connected to the city water and sewer system where available as determined by the city.
B. Private wells for residential or commercial use are prohibited inside the city limits.
(Prior Code, § 37-001)
701:
A. When a property owner requests utility services to property not within the corporate city limits, at the discretion of the city, the owner will be required to:
1. Petition for annexation, if the property is contiguous to the existing city limits, prior to commencement of construction of utility lines; or
2. Execute a restrictive covenant consenting to annexation of such property into the city when the property becomes contiguous.
B. When such property is not contiguous and execution of the covenant is required, the owner will also be required to submit a certificate of title to the city attorney to verify ownership of the property. The covenant will be recorded in the property records at the county courthouse and will stipulate that, if the property becomes contiguous in the future and the property owner refuses to petition for annexation, the city will have the authority to terminate utility services.
C. Construction of utility lines will not begin until the requirements of this policy are met, which shall be indicated by authorization of the mayor and council.
(Prior Code, § 37-002)
702:
A. All water and sewer connections shall be executed by city personnel. Water and sewer connection fees shall be as determined from time to time.
B. Any other dimensions for water and sewer connections not addressed in this section shall be determined on an as needed basis by the public works director.
C. The city reserves the right to negotiate connection fees based on special circumstances as determined by the city for commercial and industrial consumers and for residential connections when applications are for a two inch water meter or larger.
D. Notwithstanding any other provision to the contrary in this article, a commercial development or an apartment complex may utilize a master water meter and be billed by the city for the entire development or complex, provided said development or complex has more than four units. A holder of a master water meter may meter and require its tenants to meter individual usage and reimburse the holder of the master meter for water and sewer usage; provided, however, said reimbursement shall not exceed the cost of the water or sewer paid to the city by the master meter holder.
(Prior Code, § 37-003)
703:
Once availability of service is determined and connection fees are paid, the consumer shall make application for service at city hall. A picture ID is required of the person making application. If it is determined the applicant has an outstanding balance, payment in full of that balance must be paid before service shall commence.
(Prior Code, § 37-004)
704:
All individuals (residential and commercial) applying for service shall at the time of application pay a security deposit.
(Prior Code, § 37-005)
705:
The water, sewer, and sprinkler/irrigation rates and criteria are as determined from time to time by ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 37-006; Ord. of 6-9-2009; Ord. of 8-11-2009; Ord. of 10-14-2008; Ord. of 7-14-2010, § 37-006)
706:
A. Bills shall be mailed the last business day of each month with a billing date of the first day of the following month.
B. A ten percent penalty charge based on unpaid balances will be assessed the next business day after the tenth of each month. In the event the tenth day of the month falls on a nonbusiness day, the next business day will be considered the tenth day and penalties will accrue the day after.
C. A delinquent charge as determined from time to time by ordinance will be assessed to each account that remains unpaid after the 20th of each month, at which point service is subject to disconnection. In the event the 20th day of the month falls on a nonbusiness day, the next business day will be considered the 20th day and the delinquent charge will accrue the day after.
D. Failure to receive bills or notices shall not prevent bills from becoming delinquent nor relieve the consumer from payment of the bill or any subsequent late charges.
(Prior Code, § 37-007)
707:
A. Not less than three days' notice shall be given, in person or in writing, at city hall to discontinue service or to transfer service to another location. The outgoing party shall be responsible for all water consumed up to the time of departure or the time specified for departure, whichever period is longer. The new occupant shall apply for service within 48 hours after occupying the premises and failure to do so will make such person liable for paying for the service furnished since the last meter reading.
B. A transfer fee shall be collected at such time when a customer chooses to relocate service from one location to another within the city's water and sewer system.
C. In the event that the customer does not have a sufficient deposit amount on an active account as described in section 36-023, payment of such shall be made at this time. In addition, any information required as described in section 36-022 that is not on file shall be provided as well.
(Prior Code, § 37-008)
708:
A. Sprinkler meters are for the specific purpose of outdoor watering only. Fees for sprinkler meter connections inside and outside the city limits are as determined from time to time.
B. Any other dimensions for sprinkler meters not addressed in this section shall be determined on an as needed basis by the public works director.
C. The city reserves the right to negotiate connection fees based on special circumstances as determined by the city for commercial and industrial consumers and for residential connections when applications are for a two inch meter or larger.
D. Sprinkler meters shall be installed per work order when payment is made in full for the meter. Once the meter is installed monthly charges shall commence. Billing for sprinkler meters shall be for 12 months of every year for existing sprinkler meters as well as for new connections. Billing charges shall be the minimum charge plus any additional charges that may be applicable based on consumption.
E. In order for monthly charges not to be incurred, one of the two following options must occur:
1. Notification in writing by the consumer to the city that the meter is no longer needed and removal of the meter is requested. If for any reason in the future the consumer wishes to have the meter reinstalled, a fee as determined from time to time by ordinance will be charged. The meter will then be reinstalled upon payment of the fee and monthly billing on the meter will resume.
2. Notification in writing by the consumer to the city that the consumer wishes to have the meter to remain installed but locked by city personnel there will be a cut off fee when the meter is locked and a cut on fee when the consumer wishes to have the meter unlocked. Once the meter is unlocked billing on the meter will resume.
(Prior Code, § 37-009)
709:
A. The city shall run a water service line from its distribution line to the property line where the distribution line exists or is to be constructed and runs immediately adjacent and parallel to the property to be served. No service charge, other than the connection fee referred to in sections 36-021 and 36-027 will be made for a three-fourths-inch meter. A proportionately greater charge than the connection fee will be made for a meter of larger dimensions.
B. The city may make connections to service other properties not adjacent to its lines upon payment of reasonable costs for the extensions of its distribution lines as may be required to render such service.
C. The city may install its meter at or near the property line or at the city's option, on the consumer's property within three feet of the property line.
D. The city reserves the right to refuse water and sewer service unless the consumer's lines or pipings are installed in such a manner as to prevent cross connections or backflow.
E. Under normal conditions, the consumer will be notified of any anticipated interruptions of service by the city.
(Prior Code, § 37-010)
710:
A. Water furnished by the city shall be used for consumption by the consumer, members of the consumer's household and employees only. Except as provided in section 36-021, the consumer shall not sell water to any other person or permit any other person to use such water. Water shall not be used for irrigation, fire protection, or other purposes, except when water is available in sufficient quantity without interfering with the regular domestic consumption in the area served. Disregard for this rule shall be sufficient cause for refusal or discontinuance of service.
B. Where the meter or meter box is placed on the premises of a consumer, a suitable place shall be provided by the consumer therefor, unobstructed and accessible at all times to the meter reader.
C. The consumer shall furnish and maintain a private cutoff valve on the consumer's side of the meter as well as a backflow preventor.
D. The consumer's piping and apparatus shall be installed and maintained by the consumer at the consumer's expense, in a safe and efficient manner, and in accordance with the sanitary regulations of the state board of health.
E. In order to be received as a consumer and entitled to receive water from the city's water system, all applicants must offer proof that any private wells located on their property are not physically connected to the lines of the city's covenant and agree that, so long as they continue to be consumers of the city they will not permit the connection of any private wells on their property to the city's water system.
F. It shall be unlawful for any person to tap, connect with, disturb, damage, turn on or off any main, service connection or meter of any public utility in the city, whether such device is within the public ways or on private premises, unless such person is acting by the consent of or under direction of the utility owning such property.
1. Proof that any appliances, tools, devices or instruments of any kind have been used to improperly pass water around the meter so as to prevent the meter from duly registering shall constitute prima facie evidence of the commission or the intent to commit the acts described in subsection F. of this section.
2. Where there is no evidence to the contrary, the following shall be presumed to be responsible for the illegal act set forth in subsection F. of this section:
a. The person performing any of the illegal acts;
b. The person who, with knowledge of such violation, receives the benefit of such service without proper charge as a result of the improper action; and
c. The person in whose name the utilities are in at the time of the illegal act.
The consequences of such illegal acts shall be criminal charges imposed by the Butler Police Department and fines to be collected from such charges to be determined by the city's municipal court judge.
(Prior Code, § 37-011)
711:
A. Duly authorized agents of the city shall have access at all hours to the premises of the consumer for the purpose of installing or removing city property; inspecting piping, reading and testing meters; or for any other purpose in connection with the utility service and its facilities.
B. Extensions to the system shall be made only when the consumer shall grant or convey or shall cause to be granted or conveyed to the city a permanent easement or right-of-way across any property traversed by the water and or sewer lines.
(Prior Code, § 37-012)
712:
The minimum charge, as provided in the utility rate schedules, shall be made for such connection subscribed for. Utility service furnished for a given lot shall be used on that lot only, and, except for water or fire protection, the city shall not under any condition furnish utility service free of charge to anyone.
(Prior Code, § 37-013)
714:
Charges will be filed if meter is tampered with in any way. Charge will be a minimum of $1,000.00. Services will not be connected/reconnected until the $1,000.00 and balance of bill is paid in full.
(Ord. of 5-10-2016)
715:
Only two allowed per year; delinquent fee is applied.
(Ord. of 5-10-2016)
716:
No services will be connected or disconnected after 4:00 p.m. If services must be cut off/on, the on-call employee will receive two hours overtime.
(Ord. of 5-10-2016)
